title: Wallpaper Removal & Wall Prep | Gainesville & Ocala FL
description: Wallpaper removal in Gainesville, Ocala, and North Central Florida: paper and glue removed, torn drywall skimmed, walls sealed, primed, and painted.
h1: Wallpaper Removal and Paint-Ready Wall Prep
heroIntro: We strip old paper and borders, wash off every trace of adhesive, repair the drywall underneath, and leave walls sealed and painted. No bubbling paint a month later.

sections.h2: When wallpaper needs to come off
body: Wallpaper from the 1980s and 1990s is still hanging in plenty of North Central Florida bathrooms, kitchens, and dining rooms. Some of it is peeling at the seams from years of humidity; some is simply out of style. Either way, wallpaper removal is the first step toward clean painted walls, and it is the step most often rushed.

Painting over paper is tempting, but it rarely ends well. Seams telegraph through the paint, water-based primers can soften the paste and lift the paper, and the next person who wants a change faces a harder job. We remove it properly instead.

We also see wallpaper in rentals and recently purchased homes where the new owner wants a neutral start. In those cases removal is often scheduled before move-in, when rooms are empty and the work goes fastest.

Older homes sometimes hide a second surprise: paper hung over paneling or plaster. Those walls need a different approach, and the crew lead will note it on the walkthrough so the method and any extra prep are spelled out before you approve the job.
bullets: Full-wall vinyl, paper, and grasscloth coverings
Borders at ceiling and chair-rail height
Bathroom and kitchen paper loosened by steam and humidity
Multiple layers hung over each other through the years

sections.h2: Removing the paper without wrecking the wall
body: Every wall is tested before work begins. Some strippable papers release dry once a corner is lifted. Others need scoring, a warm enzyme solution, or steam to soften the paste behind the face. The method is picked for the paper and the wall, because too much water on drywall swells the board and too little leaves you scraping for hours.

Floors, outlets, and trim are protected, and switch plates come off. Crews peel the face layer, soak the backing, and lift it off with wide flexible knives held at a low angle to avoid gouging. For a homeowner-level look at the process, our article on removing wallpaper without damaging drywall explains the same principles.

sections.h2: Glue residue is the real problem
body: Getting the paper off is the easy half. Leftover adhesive is what ruins the paint job. It looks invisible once it dries, but it stays slightly tacky, reactivates in humid weather, and makes fresh paint crack, wrinkle, or blister weeks after the crew is gone. If you have ever seen bubbling paint on drywall in a former wallpapered room, this is often why.

Walls are washed repeatedly with warm water and a cleaner until a hand drawn across the surface comes away clean and squeaks. Then the wall is sealed with an oil-based or specialty primer made to lock down any residue we could not see. Ordinary latex primer is not used at this stage, because water can reactivate the glue underneath it.

sections.h2: Torn face paper, skim coats, and repairs
body: When wallpaper was hung directly on unprimed drywall, the paste bonds to the board's paper face. No technique fully prevents some tearing in that situation. Torn spots expose brown kraft paper that bubbles if painted directly.

We plan for that from the start. Torn areas are sealed first, then skim coated and sanded smooth before priming. If an entire wall is affected, a full skim coat gives a better result than dozens of spot repairs. That step is written into the estimate, so it is not a surprise change order midway through. Bigger damage, such as soft board behind a leaking shower, goes through our drywall repair and patching service.

sections.h2: Painting the walls and planning the room
body: Once walls are sealed and repaired, they are ready for color. Bathrooms and kitchens get a washable satin or a moisture-resistant finish; dining rooms and bedrooms can take eggshell or matte. If you are not sure what color should replace a pattern you have looked at for twenty years, a short color consultation with full-size drawdowns helps. Our guide on picking a paint finish for each room covers sheen choices.

A single bathroom usually needs a few days because removal, washing, repair, primer, and two coats of paint each need dry time. Larger rooms or several layers take longer. You can stay in the home while we work room by room, and the estimate lists each wall, the removal method, the primer, and the finish so you know exactly what you are getting. Wallpaper removal often goes hand in hand with a broader interior painting project.

faqs.q: Can you paint over wallpaper instead of removing it?
faqs.a: It is possible on a well-bonded paper with an oil-based primer, but seams usually show and the paper can lift later. We recommend removal in most cases and will tell you honestly if your situation is an exception.

faqs.q: What if the drywall tears during removal?
faqs.a: Torn face paper is common when paper was hung on unprimed board. We seal it, skim coat, and sand before priming. That work is planned in the estimate rather than added later.

faqs.q: Why did paint bubble on my walls after wallpaper came off?
faqs.a: Usually because adhesive residue was left behind or torn drywall paper was painted directly. Both are fixed by washing, sealing with the right primer, and skimming damaged areas.

faqs.q: Do you remove wallpaper borders only?
faqs.a: Yes. Borders come off the same way, and the band of wall underneath is cleaned, sealed, and blended so it does not show through the new paint.
